html:
Al Ain is a group of oases on the border of Abu Dhabi and Oman, where date palms have been watered by underground channels called falaj for some three thousand years.

The channels, like the qanats of Iran and the aflaj of Oman, carry groundwater by gravity from the mountains. Some of the oldest known in Arabia, from the Iron Age, were found at Hili in Al Ain. Shares of water were owned and traded, and the date palm fed the people.

Al Ain was the home of the Al Nahyan family, and Sheikh Zayed governed it before he ruled Abu Dhabi. The oasis and nearby Bronze Age sites became a World Heritage Site in 2011.
sum: Al Ain is a group of oases on the border of Abu Dhabi and Oman, where date palms have been watered by underground channels called falaj for some three thousand years.
